full_judgment:
This revisional application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against the judgment and decree dated 15.4.85 passed by Mr. Siddiqur Rahman Mia, Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 382 of 1983 allowing the appeal reversing the judgment and decree dated 27.11.83 passed by Mr. Matiur Rahman, Munsif, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 389 of 1983. 

 4. After considering the evidence adduced by both the parties the learned Munsif, now Assistant Judge, decreed the suit and declared the order of removal passed under Memo No. 4RC/7-53/77 Admn. dated 7.3.78 by the opposite party No. 1 as void, malafide and not binding on the plaintiff and that the plaintiff was still in service. 

 5. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree passed by the learned Munsif, the opposite party No. 1 preferred Title Appeal No. 382 of 1983 and after considering the materials before him and the law involved in the case the learned Subordinate Judge reversed the judgment and decree passed by the learned Munsif by delivering the impugned judgment on 15.4.1985 and dismissed the suit. 

 8. Mr. Lutfar Rahman Majumdar, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, has tried to assail the judgment and decree of the learned Subordinate Judge on several grounds contending, first of all, that the learned Subordinate Judge, without reversing the 'finding arrived at by the Trial Court was not competent to set aside the judgment and decree of the said Court. His further contention is that the petitioner was not an employee serving under the opposite party No.1 or the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Council which is an autonomous body and was on deputation there purely on temporary basis and his lien under the Ministry of Agriculture subsisted and as such, the opposite party No.1, the Executive Vice President of Bangladesh Agricultural Research Council, was not competent to draw up any proceeding or to impose any penalty on him including removal from service. According to him, he being a Government servant the Government alone was, under the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1976 competent to impose penalty on him. His next contention appears to be that he was illegally charged at the instigation of some employees of the Bangladesh Agriculture Research Council with a view to secure his removal in order to clear their way for appointment to the post of Accounts Officer. Lastly, the learned Advocate for the petitioner has submitted that the procedure laid down in the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1976 were not allowed and the petitioner was not afforded any opportunity of arranging his defence and of cross-examining the witnesses produced by the opposite party No.1 and also of adducing evidence in his defence. He concluded by contending that the entire proceedings against the petitioner was violative of the provisions of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1976 and the principles of natural justice. 

 16. The judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge are hereby set aside and those of the learned Munsif are restored although not on the same grounds.
